newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks ends weak but Cheung Kong group rallies.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks ends weak but Cheung Kong group rallies.

text.p: Solid gains in shares of the Cheung Kong group failed to lift the overall tone in Hong Kong on Tuesday where stocks erased their early gains to end weak on concerns about higher interest rates, analysts said.

The Hang Seng index closed 23.77 points lower at 13,420.16 after being driven to a high of 13,564.60 by a reshuffle in the Cheung Kong group. Trading in the group lifted turnover to a heavy HK$13.57 billion compared with Monday's HK$11.13 billion.
"I think only the Cheung Kong group really performed well. The others just saw some heavy profit-taking," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities.
Shares in Cheung Kong, Hutchison Whampoa, Hongkong Electric and Cheung Kong Infrastructure resumed trading on Tuesday after being suspended on Monday due to the announcement of a corporate reshuffle.

Hutchison plans to make a general offer for Hongkong Electric at HK$26.50 per share and then transfer its stake in the utility to Cheung Kong Infrastructure (CKI) in exchange for new CKI shares. Cheung Kong will also transfer its 70.66 percent stake in CKI to Hutchison for about HK$20.45 billion.
Analysts said all companies in the group should benefit. Cheung Kong shares ended the day HK$5.00 higher at HK$72.75.
Hutchison advanced HK$2.75 to HK$61.25, Hongkong Electric rose HK$2.40 to HK$27.65 and Cheung Kong Infrastructure gained HK$0.10 to HK$21.25.
Despite gains in the group, property and banking stocks came under pressure on Tuesday. Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$1.50 to HK$94.25 and Henderson Land slipped HK$1.25 to HK$74.75.
HSBC Holdings shed HK$1.00 to HK$167.00 and Hang Seng Bank finished HK$1.00 lower at HK$92.25.

"A lot of people are still worried about this Friday's U.S. payrolls," said Ricky Tam, senior research analyst at Delta Asia Securities. "If this week's non-farm payrolls are a bit higher then the possibility for the Fed to increase interest rates is quite high."

Tam expected the Hang Seng index to trade in a range of 13,200 to 13,500 points this week ahead of the release of the data. Ng said stocks were just undergoing a healthy correction after a Hang Seng rise of 221 points on Monday.
Shares in Shanghai Petrochemical fell HK$0.125 to HK$2.325 after the company announced a placement of 150 million new H-shares at HK$2.28 each.
CITIC Pacific continued its decline, ending the session off HK$1.00 at HK$39.20.
